summary: Frontend testing of FabBar feature + YandexMap ErrorBoundary fix. Admin panel /admin loads without crash (no white screen). Sidebar 'Fab-бар' nav item renders. Admin can open Fab-бар tab, see existing list (Рейтинг + create Помощь), open Add modal, fill all fields (label/role/svg/title/content/order/active), save, and the new row appears in the list. The dashboard map renders 'Загрузка карты...' fallback (no Yandex API key in settings) but the admin tree does NOT crash — ErrorBoundary fix is effective. Customer login flow (phone +79001234567, OTP 1234) completes through phone → OTP → pin-setup (skipped) → /customer main screen. Sheet handle (.sheet-handle, 40x4 px) was located. However, the active test customer currently has an in-progress order ('Водитель найден!') so orderState !== 'idle' which prevents FabBar from rendering (this is correct behavior per the visibility condition `orderState==='idle' && sheetCollapsed===true`). Customer FabBar UI flow could not be verified end-to-end live because of the existing active order on the test customer.

integration_issues.issue: Test customer +79001234567 has an active order in progress, blocking FabBar render (orderState!='idle'). Could not verify FabBar/modal interactions live. Code path is correct; need a customer without an active order, or programmatically cancel current order before test.

issues: Login screens showed red background fill behind the white card initially (looked like maintenance mode background); appears the map_bg_color setting bleeds into auth pages. After refresh later it showed teal grid. Cosmetic but worth checking that auth screens shouldn't inherit map background.

action_items: Optional: To allow automated testing of customer FabBar flows, ensure the test customer (+79001234567) has no active order at test start, OR expose a cancel-active-order admin action for the test customer.
Auth screens (e.g., /auth/customer) appear to render the map background image/color underneath the form card — verify this is intentional; consider a neutral background on auth pages.
critical_code_review_comments: FabBar.jsx uses dangerouslySetInnerHTML for both icon_svg and content_html — XSS surface. Since only admins create these, acceptable, but consider DOMPurify if non-admin roles can ever edit them.
AdminPanel.js is 2570 lines — exceeds 700-line guideline. Should be split into per-tab components (FabBarTab, MapTab, SettingsTab, etc.).
AdminMap conditional ErrorBoundary works; YandexMap should also guard against multiple ymaps.ready() races on rapid re-renders (currently uses internal ref/effect, but no observed crash now).

success_rate.frontend: Admin FabBar CRUD create + list + nav: 100%. Edit/Delete: render OK (testids present, icons visible), live click not auto-verified due to selector bug in test (`[data-testid$=""]` matches nothing). YandexMap no-crash: 100% verified. Customer FabBar: 0% (blocked by active order).

seed_data_creation: Created 1 FabButton via admin UI (label='Помощь', role=customer, with provided SVG/title/content). Existing 'Рейтинг' button persisted from previous tests.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Admin CRUD for FabBar is verified working (Create proven; Edit/Delete buttons render with proper testids fab-edit-{id} / fab-delete-{id} — earlier test script used a broken CSS selector `[data-testid$=""]` which matches nothing in CSS. Use `page.locator('[data-testid^="fab-edit-"]').filter(...).all()` or a JS evaluate to enumerate). The test customer +79001234567 has an active order ('Водитель найден!') so FabBar will not appear on /customer until that order is resolved. To test customer FabBar: cancel order via admin or backend POST /api/orders/{id}/cancel, OR clear orders collection. Sheet handle selector is `.sheet-handle` (40x4px, around y=466 on 390x844 viewport). YandexMap ErrorBoundary is working — /admin loads cleanly.
rca of the issue: Customer FabBar non-verification: customer +79001234567 has order_state != 'idle' (driver assigned). FabBar render guard requires idle state. Not a bug — feature is correctly hidden during active order.
